order_reconstruction.publisher_statement_multiple_purchases:
### Multiple purchases per session

A session can have multiple **purchase** events. It's ok, because it's a single order.

decisions_needed.title: Deduplication

Same (user_session, product_id, event_type, event_time): 30221 surplus rows in 18100 groups; 1 of those groups contain rows that differ in another column.
Same (user_session, product_id, event_type) within one second: 30221 surplus rows in 18100 groups; 1 contain non-identical rows.
decisions_needed.choice_forced: Which rows count as one event before any funnel count.
options: Keep all rows as logged.
Drop exact duplicate rows only.
Collapse on (user_session, product_id, event_type, event_time).

decisions_needed.choice_forced: Whether zero, negative, or null priced purchases count toward revenue and toward purchase counts.
options: Count them as purchases and as revenue at their logged price.

options: Use the price logged on each event.

decisions_needed.title: Order definition without an order ID
evidence: Order or transaction ID columns found: none.
Sessions with at least one purchase event: 629560; with more than one: 80261.
(user_session, product_id) pairs with more than one purchase event: 41406 (52477 surplus events); pairs with repeats in the same second: 75.
Publisher statement (evidence only, not a decision), verbatim from the Kaggle dataset page: "A session can have multiple **purchase** events. It's ok, because it's a single order."
decisions_needed.choice_forced: What one order is, which determines order counts and order value.
options: One order per session that has at least one purchase event.
One order per (session, product) purchase pair.
One order per purchase event.
Purchase events grouped by user_id within a time window.
